newsitem.title: UK: Argentina's Mendoza to set dollar bond next week.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Mendoza to set dollar bond next week.

text.p: The Argentinian province of Mendoza is expected to launch a two-tranche dollar bond in the middle of next week, bankers said on Friday.
A five-year tranche was likely to be priced to yield around 250 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and a 10-year tranche was likely to yield around 350 b.p. over.
Both tranches would be for at least $100 million each, bankers said, and the total deal was expected to be for $250 million. The transaction will be unsecured.
BankBoston and Credit Suisse First Boston are joint lead managers and roadshows have already been held.
Moody's Investors Service has rated the forthcoming bond issue B1, which was not constrained by Argentina's B1 foreign currency country ceiling, it said.
Standard & Poor's assigned Mendoza a BB minus rating, compared with its BB rating for Argentina.
Mendoza is one of Argentina's 23 provinces and is located in the western part of the country along the border with Chile.
Next week's bond will be the province's second international bond issue. In 1996 it issued a $150 million bond collateralised by oil production royalties.
Also next week, the province of Corrientes was expected to launch a $112 million five-year bond via BankBoston, Banco de Galicia and Banco Rio.
The deal, to be backed by tax receivables, will be an amortising FRN with an average life around three years. Bankers said there was no price talk for the deal yet.
On Thursday the province of Tucuman launched a $200 million tax receivables-backed bond with an average life of 3.6 years, which paid 345 b.p. over Treasuries.
